exposure: resuscitation with bubble CPAP (bCPAP) with humidified gas
resuscitation with T-piece device with non-humidified gas
outcome: duration of ventilation in the first 72 hours
cohort: The study included 357 infants born at less than 32 weeks gestation, with a mean gestational age of 28 ± 2 weeks, divided into two epochs based on the resuscitation method used.
finding: Implementing bCPAP from the first breaths in infants less than 32 weeks' gestation was associated with improved short-term outcomes and reduced mortality, despite an increased incidence of chronic lung disease.
followup_time: Up to hospital discharge (with ventilation duration measured in the first 72 hours)
gest_age: Less than 32 weeks gestation (mean 28 ± 2 weeks, with a subgroup of less than 25 weeks gestation)
